chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from al-Amriki, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both), who said:

I asked him about a man who manumitted his slave by contract (mukatabah), and after making the contract he said to him: 'Give me a portion of the price, and I will expedite your manumission in place of the contract.' He asked: Is that permissible? He replied: 'If it is a gift (hiba), there is no harm; but if he said: 'Reduce [the price] for me, and I will expedite [your manumission],' then it is not valid.'

key_terms.مُكَاتَبَة: Contract of manumission where a slave pays a fixed sum in installments

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between a gift and a price reduction in Islamic slave manumission contracts?
ai.summary: Imam Musa al-Kadhim clarifies the distinction between a gratuitous gift (hiba) and a conditional reduction (hut) in the context of mukatabah, a contract where a slave pays for freedom in installments. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on the intention and structure of the transaction, ensuring that a 'gift' remains distinct from a sale-like exchange to maintain legal validity. The hadith underscores the flexibility in manumission contracts while preserving the integrity of the master-slave financial relationship.
